Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

visual.alt: An eight-stage cyclical process diagram showing glass bottles being collected from shops, sorted at the plant, stripped of labels and washed, then refilled and returned to shops; damaged bottles are separated out to be melted down.

key_points: The process is cyclical, not linear: filled bottles go to shops, empties are collected and cleaned, and refilling sends them back into the same cycle
The first three stages are about collection: delivery, the customer leaving the empty bottle at a collection point, and crates being taken by lorry to the plant
Sorting happens first at the plant; damaged bottles are removed from the cycle and melted down to make new bottles — this is the diagram's only side branch
Cleaning has two steps: labels are soaked off in a washing tank, then the bottles are rinsed with hot water and checked
Only bottles that pass inspection are refilled and capped, then returned to shops with new labels and crates
Not all eight stages take place at the plant; the customer is also part of the process, and because the cycle returns to its starting point there is no clear 'final' stage
common_mistakes: Failing to notice the cycle and ending with 'finally'; not stating that the diagram loops back to the start
Not using the passive voice (are collected, are rinsed) and instead inventing a subject for every sentence ('workers wash the bottles')
Leaving out the side branch where damaged bottles are separated
Adding information that is not in the diagram (how many bottles, how long it takes, what it costs)
Describing the stages out of order; not using linking words such as 'first / then / after that / once'
